title: Service account provisioning guardrails: naming, ownership, and audit hooks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a set of provisioning guardrails for service accounts that standardize creation, enforce ownership, and wire audit hooks into our logging pipeline. This ticket covers: 1) a template catalog that enforces allowed role combinations (no broad cluster-level roles), 2) automated naming and tagging conventions (team, environment, owner email), 3) mandatory owner assignment and escalation rules, 4) SSO/SAML mapping guidelines for automated principal binding, and 5) audit-log enrichment (creator, approver, template id, key material fingerprint) with retention tags for the console and Splunk/Datadog ingestion. Goal: reduce ad-hoc SA creation, make ownership discoverable, and ensure all SAs produce consistent audit signals for incident analysis and cost allocation.
acceptance_criteria: New SA creation flow requires selecting a template from the catalog or a justified exception with approval link
Owner field is required and must map to an LDAP/SSO group or individual; orphaned SAs flagged for review after 7 days
Templates encode least-privilege role bundles for RBAC v2 and are validated by the policy engine; any request that would grant elevated roles must create a JIRA with approver
Audit events include template_id, creator_id, approver_id (if exception), public-key-fingerprint, and template_hash and are visible in the Console activity stream within 60s
E2E tests exist for UI flow, API provisioning CLI, and audit log ingestion; tests run in CI and pass on PR
Documentation (Confluence) published: onboarding steps, how to request exceptions, and template governance process
